title: An issue's own assignee never opened a pull request that closes it
author: nisaba
description: Reads an open issue's structured `assignees` field -- GitHub's explicit, private 'you specifically are on the hook' commitment, distinct from a public label's open call -- against every pull request's own author and body, and surfaces an issue where NONE of its named assignees has ever opened a pull request naming that issue via a real closing keyword. A stranger's PR closing the issue, or the assignee's own PR closing a DIFFERENT issue, both leave this seam open; only an assignee's own PR closing THIS issue closes it.
confidence_notes: Age-gated on hours since the issue's own `created_at` -- the same documented proxy `good-first-issue-never-referenced` already uses, and for the identical reason: `ListIssues` carries no per-assignee assigned-at timestamp, only the issue's own creation time, so that is the honest clock available rather than a guess at when the assignment itself landed. Under 24 hours old scores 0.5 (below the 0.70 bar, weighed in the tail not hidden -- a same-day assignment deserves a moment before its silence reads as a gap). At or past 24 hours it scores a flat 0.85 -- reusing seam_engine.closing_keywords.closing_keyword_numbers verbatim against every pull request's own body, an unambiguous structural read once both lists are held at once, not a guess. Shorter than good-first-issue-never-referenced's 168-hour bar on purpose: an assignment is a direct, private ask of one named person, a faster human cadence than a public 'come help' label waiting for a stranger to even notice it. An issue already closed is excluded at confidence 0.0, named not hidden -- whatever happened, the working promise resolved. An issue carrying no assignees at all is never a candidate in the first place, not even named in excluded -- an unassigned issue never made this specific promise. An issue where at least one named assignee authored at least one pull request (open, closed, or merged -- an abandoned attempt still counts as a real swing taken, the same precedent good-first-issue-never-referenced already set) that names the issue via a real closing keyword is excluded at confidence 0.0, named not hidden -- the promise was kept, or at least attempted, by the person actually asked. A pull request that references the issue but was authored by someone who is NOT one of its assignees does not fulfill the promise -- a bystander's own attempt is real activity, but it is not the specific person's answer this recipe checks for.
